III p164.text: But Tragedy has a poetic design, that is, it represents an action in order to move, and to delight by the emotion.
III p164.alignment: Hempel German p. 164 and Weiss English p. 333 both contain the entire sentence: tragedy has a poetic purpose, representing an action in order to move and delight through emotion. The following historical and poetic truth discussion is outside this place.

Personally read Hempel p. 164 and the Duke copy of Weiss 1845 p. 333: the complete sentence matches the printed English, including its punctuation, and corresponds to the German poetic purpose of representing an action to move and delight through that emotion. The earlier p163 place is not included: Weiss changes showing sensuousness satisfactions into offering periodic alleviations, adding periodicity and changing the relation.
